why: A (universes 0): for a matrix group G (slice submanifold of Mₙ(𝕜), induced metric), A ∈ 𝔤, γ(t) = exp(tA), h(t) = exp(tA/2), K_A(U) = ¼[[A,U],A]: D/dt(hUh) = hU'h, R(γ',hMh)γ' = hK_A(M)h, hUh is a Jacobi field IF U'' + K_A U = 0, and its covariant derivative at 0 is U'(0). B: Theorem 20.5 on an abstract locally symmetric manifold for any geodesic on an interval and any orthonormal eigenbasis of K_V: (1) conjugate parameters = πk/√e_i, (2) multiplicities = counts of e_i, (3) parallel eigenframe and 'Σw_iP_i Jacobi ⇔ w_i'' + e_iw_i = 0'. A ⇒ B fails genuinely, also for matrix groups: A has no conjugate points or multiplicities (for SU(n) they are in SUJacobi.lean, not this item), only the 'if' half of the frame equation, only along exp(tA) through I, and no identification of the parallel frame (uniqueness of parallel transport) or of the blind K_V's eigenvalues. B ⇒ A fails: nothing about matrices, halfExp, jacK; B's local-symmetry hypothesis is not established for G in the project.
